claim: A commodity- or rate-linked stock only trades its own earnings if earnings days appear among its ten biggest single-day moves; otherwise the print is the wrong catalyst
test: For the name, rank its ten largest single-day moves over ~18 months and count how many are earnings reaction days, then compare the average absolute earnings-day move to the stock's overall volatility. Pattern HOLDS if names with 2+ earnings days in the top ten move materially on their prints while names with 0-1 do not (their average earnings-day move collapses toward ~2% despite high general ATR). FALSIFIED if a name with 0-1 earnings days in its top ten nevertheless produces repeated large, tradeable earnings reactions.

claim: A RAISED guide still gets sold when the economics underneath it deteriorate - margins compressing, losses widening, or the raise carried by a lumpy line while the recurring line stalls
test: On any raise-and-fall, read the release for (a) gross margin or EBITDA moving the WRONG way in the same quarter, or (b) the raise carried by a non-recurring line item while the recurring one is flat. Pattern HOLDS if at least one is present and the stock fell. FALSIFIED if a company raises guidance WITH improving margins AND improving recurring revenue and is still sold off - that would mean something other than unit economics is doing the work. This refines the v24 Guide Rule rather than contradicting it: the guide outranks the print, but the line items underneath outrank the guide.

claim: The AI trade splits on CASH EARNINGS NOW versus CAPEX MONETIZED LATER. As FY2027 numbers arrive, names whose multiple rests on future monetization get repriced down, while AI names already converting to earnings hold or re-rate up. Adam's call, 2026-08-14: 'the ai run has been a lot of speculation, I see next years earning wrecking some'
test: Split the AI complex into two baskets at logging: (A) EARNINGS-BACKED - positive FCF and a trailing PE under ~25 today (GOOGL 17.26 is the anchor); (B) STORY-PRICED - negative FCF, no PE, or a multiple resting on announced capex and bookings rather than delivered profit. Track the 2-day post-earnings reaction and the trailing 4-quarter return of both baskets across the FY2027 reporting cycle (roughly Q4-26 prints in Jan-2027 through Q3-27 prints in Oct-2027). PATTERN HOLDS if basket B's median post-print reaction is materially negative while basket A's is flat-to-positive, and the A-minus-B return spread is positive. PATTERN FAILS if basket B holds or extends, if the spread is flat or negative, or if the drawdown is INDISCRIMINATE - an everything-selloff that takes A down with B is a macro event, NOT this pattern, and must be recorded as holds=false. Related and already supported: P-006 and P-008 (the guide outranks the print) are the single-name mechanism this basket-level claim would operate through.

claim: A price target that exists only in a post or a note, and never as a RESTING LIMIT ORDER, does not get taken. The book's targets are not unreached because price failed to arrive - they are unreached because nothing was in the market to sell into them when it did. This is the mechanism behind P-013's observation that every closed swing exited at its stop and none ever reached Target 1: a stop is an order that lives in the market, and a target has only ever been a sentence.
test: For every logged target, record (a) whether price ever traded at or through it in ANY session, extended hours included, and (b) whether a resting limit order existed at the time. The pattern FAILS the moment a target is reached in-market with a resting order present and unfilled, or the moment the book's unreached targets are shown to be genuinely unreached by price rather than unattended.
why: Adam found this, not the framework, and he found it by asking the obvious question nobody had asked: 'you have low confidence on it why wouldn't we setup a sell price at 30 on day one'. At 55pct confidence on a binary the edge is not in the outcome, it is in the pre-event drift - and the drift has to be harvested by a mechanism, not by attention.

HOLDS if QQQ is above its own pre-shock close AND at least one layer median is positive while another layer median is negative, with the spread between the best and worst layer medians exceeding 5 percentage points. claim: A layer being REPRICED does not mean-revert on a green day: the names furthest below their pre-selloff line do not lead the bounce, the ones nearest the line do.
test: On any session the power layer median return is positive, rank the seven names by distance below their pre-selloff reference close and compare the median return of the three NEAREST the line against the three FURTHEST below it. Falsified if the three furthest below outperform the three nearest on a majority of such sessions.
why: If the layer were merely lagging, the most beaten-down names would snap back hardest - that is what mean reversion looks like. If it is being repriced by rates and merchant-power economics, the discount is information and the market keeps paying for proximity to the line, not distance from it. This separates lag from repricing on a GREEN day, when a layer-median read tells you nothing.

claim: A layer that is unanimously green while every name in it runs UNDER 1.0x volume pace is not being bought, it is being left alone - and the layer it is outperforming is red on ABOVE-normal pace, which is where the actual money is
test: On sessions where all seven power names are green at midday with every one under 1.0x time-adjusted volume pace against its 30-day average, while a majority of the buyer layer is red at ABOVE 1.0x pace, measure the power layer median return from the midday mark into the close. This separates a bid from a vacuum on exactly the day the screen makes them look identical.
